newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy Treasury seeks Autostrade buyers.
newsitem.headline: Italy Treasury seeks Autostrade buyers.

text.p: The Italian Treasury has started to put out feelers for potential investors willing to become stable shareholders in Italian motorways operator Autostrade after privatisation, the minister for public works said.
Paolo Costa told a news conference a decision on the launch date of a public share offer (OPV) to complete the company's sell-off would be made in September.

"The Treasury has already started making contact to identify the potential participants in a stable core of shareholders. In September, they will decide when to launch the OPV which will complete the privatisation," Costa said.
He noted that the timetable would be set by the Treasury and that the "first most suitable days would be from early September."
State industrial holding IRI controls 87 percent of Autostrade, which is at the top of the list for privatisation later this year. IRI is entirely controlled by the Treasury.

Costa was speaking after the signing of a convention earlier on Monday between national road maintenance company Anas and Societa Autostrade SpA. The convention defines maintenance and tariff rules for future owners of Autostrade.
"With the signing of this agreement, from this moment on we know exactly what is up for sale," Costa said.

The agreement maintains that for the next five years tariff rises must be in line with forecast inflation plus a possible 0.5 percent "so long as there is a series of increases in quality," Costa said.
